title: Red Wine Braised Chuck Roast
summary: Chuck roast seared hard, then braised in red wine and beef broth until it shreds. Rustic sauce with the vegetables left in, spooned over mashed potatoes.
authenticity_note: Built on the boeuf bourguignon method: hard sear, tomato paste and flour cooked into the fond, wine reduced before the broth goes in.
shopping_note: Pantry items are marked to confirm. Everything else is a buy.

items.name: Boneless chuck roast
items.note: Look for even marbling and a thick piece.

items.name: Dry red wine
items.note: Cabernet or Merlot you would drink. Skip cooking wine.

equipment.name: Dutch oven, 6 qt
equipment.note: A smaller pot needs the roast cut into more pieces.

prep.intro: Most of this dish is oven time. Start about 4 hours before dinner.

timeline.task: Pull the roast from the fridge. Chop vegetables.
Oven on to 325°F. Sear the beef.

concurrent: Make the mashed potatoes during the last 30 minutes of the braise.

steps.title: Chop the vegetables
instructions: Cut carrots and celery into 1-inch chunks. Big pieces survive 3 hours in the oven.
Smash the garlic cloves with the flat of the knife and peel.

warnings: Pat the beef **completely dry** before searing. Wet meat steams and never browns.

steps.title: Season and sear the beef
instructions: Pat the beef dry and season all sides with the salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in the Dutch oven until it shimmers.
Sear 4 to 5 minutes per side without moving it. Work in batches so pieces don't touch.
Move the beef to a plate.
steps.done_when: Every side has a deep brown crust. Pale gray means it needs more time.
tips: If the meat sticks, it is not ready to flip. It releases once the crust forms.

steps.title: Build the base
instructions: Lower the heat. Add onions, carrots and celery. Cook 5 minutes, scraping the bottom.
Add garlic, tomato paste and flour. Stir 1 to 2 minutes until the paste turns brick red.

howto.title: Cook out the flour
steps: Stir constantly so the flour coats the vegetables.
It should smell toasty, not raw. This is what thickens the sauce later without extra work.

steps.title: Deglaze and braise
instructions: Pour in the wine and scrape up every browned bit. Simmer 3 minutes.
Add broth, Worcestershire, Dijon and herbs.
Return the beef and plate juices. Liquid should come halfway up the meat.
steps.done_when: A fork twists into the meat with no resistance.

steps.title: Shred and finish
instructions: Remove bay leaves and herb stems. Skim fat off the top.
Shred the beef in the pot with two forks.
If the sauce is thin, simmer uncovered 10 minutes. Salt to taste.

plating: Wide shallow bowl. Mashed potatoes first, swooped with the back of a spoon to make a well.
Spoon beef and vegetables into the well, then extra sauce over the top.
Finish with chopped parsley or thyme leaves for color.
tips: Leftovers taste better the next day.

fixes.fix: It needs more time, not less. Back in for 30 minutes.

cooks.notes: Rich sauce. Boxed mash worked fine.
